interpretation: A first-level representative assembly with autonomous power to enact generally binding regional norms affecting rights or obligations, together with budget and executive-scrutiny powers, can qualify. Sovereignty, a federal constitution and the English label Act are not required. Municipalities remain outside the geographic scope, even where national law gives them similar ordinance powers. This does not make every regional council eligible.

authority_decisions.relationship: First-level prefecture of Japan; not a sovereign or federal state.
authority_decisions.reason: The prefectural assembly exercises substantive autonomous ordinance-making, budget and executive-scrutiny powers. Its ordinances can impose obligations and restrict rights and can provide penalties within statutory limits. This goes beyond meeting administration or a specific delegated service rule. The same statutory framework also covers municipalities; those remain outside the agreed geographic scope.

authority_decisions.relationship: Provinces of the European Netherlands; separate from the Kingdom's constituent countries and Caribbean public bodies.
authority_decisions.reason: The councils have autonomous provincial ordinance-making powers, initiative and amendment rights, budget authority and executive accountability/inquiry powers. Binding rules can apply directly to residents and businesses. National-law limits and the term verordening do not negate legislative authority. Municipal councils also have ordinance powers but remain outside the geographic scope.
